summary: This is a sound A/B arm: it adds only the measured v3 fused pre-attention (from job 825baa03798f431a) to the partner restack on full decode 1<B<=64, and it is rules-clean. The expected gain is about 1.4 us at decode_16 and 3.7 us at decode_32. That is at the cross-job drift band, so read the result from the in-process interleaved gate timing and the kernel rows, not from the headline or a row-vs-row comparison with the partner run.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. On master's profile, full decode_16/32 spend 2.0 and 2.2 us in _pre_attention_kernel next to splitkv_attn_sk_kernel<4,true> (110.1 and 225.6 us). Floors are 63.2 and 126.4 us, so the attention kernel, not pre-attn, is what dominates the distance to the floor. v3 already ran on the stage-2 kernel, which is master's variant 0 at 1<B<=64. It passed 16/16 tests, measured 110.91->109.55 and 226.81->223.11 us, and its in-process diag showed 118.2->115.1 (1.027x) and 227.7->220.5 (1.033x). The direction (faster on full decode_16/32, flat everywhere else beyond the partner's own moves) matches TASK.md: weight 16 on both, full decode_1 unchanged on the two-level path. Headline impact is about +0.9% on load decode_16 and +1.25% on load decode_32, roughly 0.35% geomean, which is far inside the ±1.5% CI. The s3 run labelled its own 1.75% and 2.4% row moves 'flat'. WEAKEST LINK: one okc run cannot show that v3 beats the partner on the full rows, because the expected per-row delta (1.2-1.6%) equals the cross-job noise band. The only clean attribution is the gate's interleaved graph-replay pair ([pre-attn + v2] vs [v3], same process, same GPU, cold L2), printed in PATH CHOSEN. Second weakest: the 1.02x gate margin sits close to v3's measured 1.027x at B=16, so prepare-time noise may gate the B=2..16 band off. That is acceptable, but then that band of this run just replicates the partner. Third: the port is a re-implementation, not the measured code. s3 built v3 as a separate kernel (splitkv_attn_sk_fused_kernel) in its own module, muse_full_decode_splitkv_v3. This spec instead folds it in as a FUSED_PRE template flag on master's splitkv_attn_sk_kernel, which also carries the partner's PSEUDO flag and the TWO flag. The kernel already uses 121 of 128 registers at __launch_bounds__(THREADS,2), and s3's audit had to restructure the q build into two smem passes to avoid spills. If the template port changes register allocation or inlining, the measured 3-7 us can disappear. Print regs/local for the FUSED_PRE instantiation and compare them with s3's [sk3] attrs line before reading timing.
confounders: full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (master c3c1b01): it owns template variant 3 (<4,true,true>, the B=1 two-level) and the existing '[sk3]' log tag (submission.py:1435, 2043). The s3 branch also called its fused kernel 'v3' with an '[sk3]' tag. Name the new instantiation and its log lines distinctly (e.g. variant 4 / '[skF]'), or the 'variants 0-3 IDENTICAL' check and PATH CHOSEN grep will point at the wrong kernel. Its self-resetting ticket arrays are shared, so the v3 self-check must re-zero them in finally (as s3 did) before the timed path runs.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv / s2 stream-K v2 (master variant 0): this is v3's comparison base. v3 was measured against exactly this kernel, so that pairing holds. But if the FUSED_PRE port perturbs codegen for variant 0 (shared device helpers, inlining changes), the [pre-attn + v2] side of the gate moves too, and both runs' full rows drift. The IDENTICAL attrs print is the guard.

fused-preattention-triton (+ paired-heads-launch-cleanup / ab-tune-batch-gate): _pre_attention_kernel is the reference math for v3, run with ROPE=False on full layers and an unpaired q layout on the gated path. A mismatch makes the self-check fall back silently to v2, and the run then measures the partner again. Grep PATH CHOSEN first.

partner restack-sk-pseudo-b1-cluster-c16-c4 (not landed, same batch): its PSEUDO edits the same kernel template and its build ladder (-DSK_PSEUDO=1 with a landed-only rebuild fallback). If this run's combined build fails and falls back to landed-only, it drops PSEUDO and the cluster routes as well as v3, so the sliding rows stop pairing. Make the fallbacks independent: drop FUSED_PRE first, then PSEUDO.
sliding-* landed hypotheses: v3 gates these shapes out. Sliding rows should match the partner's within noise, and any larger difference there is build/fallback confounding, not v3.
interference: No companion. The A/B partner (restack-sk-pseudo-b1-cluster-c16-c4) is already this change minus v3, and the instructions forbid a duplicate. Reverting a landed hypothesis isolates nothing, because no landed change shares v3's prologue; s3 already measured it against the same v2 base. The residual ambiguity is that a ~1.5% full-row difference between two jobs is noise-level. The fix is in-process, not another okc run. PATH CHOSEN must print, for each band, the interleaved graph-replay times of [pre-attn + v2] and [FUSED_PRE], plus the FUSED_PRE kernel-alone vs v2 kernel-alone time. Read the profile's top_kernels per job: whether _pre_attention_kernel disappears on full decode_16/32, and the attention kernel's own µs vs the partner's. If the gate rejects both bands, treat this run as a free replicate of the partner (a noise estimate), not as evidence against v3.
rules_flags: No rule problems found. The cache row is written in-kernel as an output (FP8 e4m3), q is FP8 E4M3 at the coarsest, merges are fp32, every key is attended (the owning CTA stores, fences and syncs before its first ring cp.async), kernel_fn does a single shape-only launch, and nothing is cached from inputs.

Correctness rests on an input-structure invariant, cache_loc[b] == page_table[b, seq_b-1], so that exactly one CTA owns the new key. reference.py builds inputs that way and s3 passed 16/16, but keep the prepare-time ownership assertion. A violation would be a silent stale-key read, not a crash.
Two-state rotation: v3 must not keep the qkv pointer or any state-sized buffer in a module/static global. Pass everything per call, as s3 did.

Compile budget: master TU + PSEUDO + the cluster TU + FUSED_PRE (s3 alone added ~40 s at import) must fit the 15-minute limit with the self-checks and gate timings. Prefer a single TU build with all flags over separate modules.
open_questions: Template flag vs separate module: s3's measured kernel lived in its own module. Folding it into master's template is cleaner long-term but is untested code on a 121/128-register kernel. Is the template port worth the risk compared with porting s3's module verbatim and keeping its own [skF] attrs line?

Should the gate margin for B=2..16 be 1.01x instead of 1.02x, given that v3's diag showed only 1.027x at B=16 and prepare timings undercount the judge by 20-25%? As written, the band may flip on noise.
If both runs pass, which one to submit should be decided by the in-process gate numbers and the full-row kernel µs, not by the two headlines, which differ by ~0.35% expected.
The larger remaining tail on this kernel is the ~6 us serialized ticket merge (s2 diag), not pre-attn. A fused-pre + two-level merge at B=16 (nseg ~17) is the natural next stage.
